<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study compared the sustained effects of interrupting sedentary behavior (SB) with short walking bouts versus a duration‐matched continuous bout on glucose homeostasis in adults with overweight/obesity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Thirty participants (16F/14M, 34 ± 7 years, 29.5 ± 3.2 kg/m
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      ) were randomized to 45 min/day of brisk walking, 5 days/week for 6 weeks, performed either as short bouts throughout the day (BREAK) or a single continuous bout (ONE). Total SB/physical activity (accelerometry) and energy expenditure (doubly labeled water) changed similarly across groups, but only BREAK reduced prolonged sitting. Insulin sensitivity (intravenous glucose tolerance test [IVGTT]) and glucose excursions (continuous glucose monitoring) were measured before and after the interventions. Group‐by‐time interactions were tested using linear mixed models.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Although neither intervention enhanced insulin sensitivity (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.366), BREAK produced more favorable changes in IVGTT‐derived glucose AUC (−1652.9 mg/dL min
                      <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                      [−2985.7, −320.1]) and glucose tolerance index (K
                      <jats:sub>G</jats:sub>
                      ; 0.54%/min [−0.01%, 1.09%]) compared with ONE. BREAK also improved free‐living daily time in range (82%–94%, odds ratio: 7.2 [1.1, 46.1]), coefficient of variation (−4.4% [−7.9%, −0.8%]), and average daily risk ratio (−9.4 [−16.4, −2.3]) relative to ONE.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Despite similar total active dose, interrupting prolonged SB with frequent active breaks produced more favorable changes in glucose tolerance and glycemic variability, but not insulin sensitivity, than a single continuous bout.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Trial Registration</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="http://clinicaltrials.gov">ClinicalTrials.gov</jats:ext-link>
                      NCT02998892
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Interrupting Prolonged Sitting Improves Glucose Regulation More Than Continuous Walking in Adults With Overweight/Obesity
